research_question: What is the effect of structured exercise training (aerobic, resistance, combined or other structured exercise, delivered during or between dialysis sessions), compared with no exercise/usual care or placebo (sham/stretching) exercise, on lower-limb functional strength measured by the timed five-repetition sit-to-stand test (seconds) in adults receiving maintenance haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis?
treatment_label: Structured exercise training (aerobic, resistance, combined or other; intradialytic or interdialytic)
control_label: No exercise / usual care or placebo (sham or stretching) exercise
outcome_description: Time in seconds to complete the five-repetition (or five-to-ten repetition) timed sit-to-stand test at the end of the exercise intervention, extracted as mean, SD and number of participants per arm. End-of-intervention values preferred; change-from-baseline (mean change and SD of change) used for both arms if only those are reported. SE/SEM converted to SD (SD = SE × √n). Repetition-count tests (30-second or 60-second sit-to-stand), timed up-and-go and six-minute walk test are not this outcome.
positive_direction: A positive effect favours exercise: participants in the exercise group complete the five-repetition sit-to-stand test in less time (shorter seconds = better lower-limb functional strength) than controls. In raw mean-difference terms this corresponds to MD < 0 seconds (exercise minus control).
search_queries: intradialytic exercise training randomized controlled trial sit-to-stand test hemodialysis
resistance or aerobic exercise dialysis patients physical function five repetition sit to stand seconds trial
peritoneal dialysis exercise program lower limb muscle strength functional capacity randomized trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults receiving maintenance dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis), including theses/dissertations reporting a randomised trial
Compares a structured exercise training programme (any mode, during or between dialysis sessions) with no exercise/usual care or placebo (sham/stretching) exercise
Reports quantitative data for a timed sit-to-stand test measured in seconds (five-repetition or five-to-ten repetition), e.g. mean and SD/SE per arm or statistics convertible to an effect size
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, protocol or purely theoretical paper)

No comparison between an exercise condition and a non-exercise/placebo control condition (e.g. control group performs a different active exercise or receives another active intervention), or non-randomised design

No quantitative outcome data permitting effect-size computation for the timed sit-to-stand test in seconds (e.g. only 30-second/60-second repetition counts, only p-values without means/SDs/SEs or n per arm)
Population unrelated to the research topic (kidney transplant recipients, non-dialysis chronic kidney disease, paediatric samples) or outcome unrelated to lower-limb sit-to-stand performance
moderators_to_extract: Programme duration in weeks and session frequency
Control type (usual care/no exercise vs placebo/sham or stretching)
Dialysis modality (haemodialysis vs peritoneal dialysis) and mean age
Sample size category and outcome data type (end value vs change score)
effect_size_note: Pool as raw mean difference (MD) in seconds with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML), reported as exercise minus control; negative MD favours exercise. Use end-of-intervention means and SDs; if only change scores are available use change mean and SD of change for both arms and flag it. Convert SE/SEM to SD using SD = SE × √n, checking table footnotes for whether "±" denotes SD or SE. Combine multiple exercise arms into a single exercise group (pooled means/SDs, summed n) and use a shared control group only once to avoid double counting.
